questions.prompt: If f(x) = 3x and g(x) = x − 4, find (f + g)(x).
If f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = 2x, find (f − g)(x).
If f(x) = x + 2 and g(x) = x − 2, find (f · g)(x).
If f(x) = x² − 9 and g(x) = x + 3, find (f/g)(x).
questions.explanation: (x² − 9)/(x + 3) = (x + 3)(x − 3)/(x + 3) = x − 3. The value x = −3 stays excluded even though the factor cancels.

questions.prompt: The notation [f ∘ g](x) means:
questions.explanation: [f ∘ g](x) = f[g(x)]: evaluate g first, then use that output as the input of f.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 5, find [f ∘ g](x).
If f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 5, find [g ∘ f](x).
questions.explanation: g[f(x)] = g(2x) = 2x + 5. Note this differs from [f ∘ g](x) = 2x + 10.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x − 1, find [f ∘ g](x).
If f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = x², find [g ∘ f](x).
Is [f ∘ g](x) always equal to [g ∘ f](x)?
choices: No, the order changes the result in general
Only when both have the same domain
questions.explanation: Composition is not commutative. It is equal only in special cases, such as when f and g are inverses.

questions.prompt: For f(x) = 4x² − 2x + 3 and g(x) = −x + 5, which value must be excluded from (f/g)(x)?
questions.explanation: Set the denominator to zero: −x + 5 = 0 gives x = 5.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = −x² + 3x + 1 and g(x) = 2x² − 5, find (f + g)(x).
If f(x) = −x² + 3x + 1 and g(x) = 2x² − 5, find (f − g)(x).
If f(x) = x² + 2x − 8 and g(x) = x² + 8, find (f ∘ g)(x).
If f(x) = x² and g(x) = 3x, find (f · g)(2).
If f(x) = x + 1 and g(x) = x², find [f ∘ g](3).
questions.explanation: Work inside out: g(3) = 9, then f(9) = 10.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = x + 1 and g(x) = x², find [g ∘ f](3).
questions.explanation: f(3) = 4, then g(4) = 16 — note this differs from [f ∘ g](3).

questions.prompt: For (f/g)(x), which values must be excluded from the domain?
questions.explanation: Division by zero is undefined, so the zeros of the DENOMINATOR are excluded.

questions.prompt: If f(x) = 2x − 1 and g(x) = x + 4, find [f ∘ g](x).
If f(x) = √x and g(x) = x − 9, what is the domain of [f ∘ g](x)?
questions.explanation: You need g(x) ≥ 0 for the square root, so x − 9 ≥ 0.
